parsed.explanation: The operative trans-facing law is absent: no presentation offence, no facility or custody rule, no documented police targeting of gender-nonconforming people. The new same-sex-conduct statute is a secondary factor (rule 2), but it is fresh, enacted unanimously under military rule amid a broader crackdown, carries 2–5 years' imprisonment, and explicitly prescribes deportation of foreigners — a stated traveller-facing consequence for a trans visitor whose relationship is read as same-sex. It is discretionary rather than demonstrated: no arrests as of late September 2025, and no enforcement record exists. The dossier is thin, so I extrapolate from structure: an actively hostile military regime, criminalisation enacted over civil-society objection, no anti-discrimination coverage, no violence-response mechanism, and pre-criminalisation records of societal abuse with religious disapproval — worse than a dead-letter statute in a tolerant society (0.65-C), but well short of documented targeting or unremedied universal exposures (0.35 tier). Open questions (entry document practice, custody, care access) are unresolved in a state with no recourse. This sits in elevated risk at the upper edge: consequence on outing is moderate-to-severe, probability drivers are social/state hostility, but no trans-specific enforcement or institutional exclusion is documented.
